title: From Fabric to Cloud: Modernizing a 15-Year-Old ERP with S/4HANA Fashion
author: SarhanP
text:
Moving from a 15-year-old SAP ECC system to RISE with SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition is a major step for a garment manufacturing company. Here is a simple and clear guide to the biggest challenges you will face and how to solve them: 1. The Industry System Change (Moving to Modern Fashion ERP) 
 The Challenge: In your old system, you probably use old SAP apparel tools (like AFS or FMS) to manage colors, sizes, and fits. S/4HANA does not support these old tools anymore. It uses a brand-new, modern system called S/4HANA Fashion and Vertical Business . 
 The Solution: Do not just copy your old system. It is much better to start fresh ( Greenfield approach ) or choose a Selective Data Transition . This allows you to redesign your color and size processes using SAP’s newest fashion standards. 2. 15 Years of "Data Garbage" 
 The Challenge: Operating for 15 years means your database is full of old, unused information (like old fabric codes, closed orders, and past customers). S/4HANA runs on a very fast but expensive memory database (HANA). The more data you move, the higher your monthly cloud subscription bill will be. 
 The Solution: Data Cleaning & Archiving. Before you move to the cloud, delete what you do not need and archive the rest. Only move active data—like current stocks, open orders, and active suppliers—to the new bulut (cloud) system. 3. Too Many Custom Codes (Z-Transactions) 
 The Challenge: Over the past 15 years, your team has likely written a lot of custom ABAP codes (Z-codes) for specific tasks like fabric cutting plans or outsourcing tracking. Many of these custom codes will not work on S/4HANA because the underlying database structure has completely changed. 
 The Solution: Keep the Core Clean. Use a tool called SAP Readiness Check to see which custom codes you actually need. You will find that S/4HANA now does many of these things automatically. For the custom features you absolutely must keep, build them outside the main ERP using the SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) . 4. Tracking Outsourced Production (Fason) 
 The Challenge: In garment manufacturing, outsourcing work (like sewing, cutting, or embroidery) is critical. Your team is used to old ECC screens to track these sub-contractors. Switching to S/4HANA changes how production planning and stock tracking look and feel. 
 The Solution: Adopt SAP Fiori. Replace the old, complicated SAP desktop screens with modern, user-friendly SAP Fiori web applications . Fiori makes tracking outsourced production much easier on phones, tablets, and modern web browsers. 5. Employee Resistance to Change 
 The Challenge: Your employees have been clicking the exact same buttons for 15 years. When you change their system, they will naturally complain that the new system is "too difficult" or "too different." 
 The Solution: Change Management & Training. Do not wait until the system is finished to show it to your team. Involve your key users on day one. Show them how new AI features (like the Joule assistant) will save them time, and provide plenty of hands-on training. 📋 Quick Summary Roadmap 
 Step 1: Scan: Run SAP Readiness Check to find your old codes and data size. 
 Step 2: Clean: Delete 15 years of old data before moving. 
 Step 3: Standardize: Stop using old custom codes; use modern SAP Fashion features instead. 
 Step 4: Train: Teach your team how to use the new Fiori screens early.

title: Beat the Single Exclusive Queue Bottleneck : Key-Based JMS Partitioning in SAP Cloud Integration
author: Aman_V
text:
Beat the Single Exclusive Queue Bottleneck 
 Key-based JMS partitioning in SAP Cloud Integration — stay in order and process fast 
 Every integration developer meets this wall sooner or later: "these messages must be processed in order." The easy fix — a single exclusive queue: one consumer, one message at a time — works perfectly and scales terribly. The moment volume rises, that single ordered lane becomes the bottleneck everything queues behind. 
 Sound familiar? How many times have you "solved" ordering by throttling everything down to one-at-a-time, then watched the backlog grow? 
 Here's the good news: you almost never need global order. You need order per key . Once you see that, you can keep strict ordering and run in parallel — on plain JMS, no premium add-ons. Let's build the idea up from scratch.

title: SAP Cloud ERP - KDM exchange rate difference leaves temporary balance on WRX/GR-IR at month-end
author: edoymaner
text:
Dear Community, 
 We are using SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition with Material Ledger / Actual Costing. 
 We are currently performing the August 2026 month-end closing and have observed an issue with our GR/IR (WRX) account for foreign currency purchase orders. Our purchase orders (PO) can have multiple line items, and the dates of goods receipt and invoice receipt are not always in the same month. 
 For example, a purchase order may have the following situation: 
 Purchase order start: August 2026 
 Purchase order end: September 2026 
 Some items have both Goods Receipt (GR) and Invoice Receipt (IR) in August 
 Some other items have GR in August but IR in September 
 Some items have both GR and IR in September 
 The issue is that even for an individual item where the GR and IR quantities are completely matched within August, a balance still remains on the GR/IR (WRX) account at the end of August. 
 We have identified that this remaining balance is related to the KDM transaction/event key (exchange rate difference). 
 For example, for one item: 
 Goods Receipt 
 WRX: Credit 1,484,178.26 TRY 
 Invoice Receipt 
 WRX: Debit 1,480,263.76 TRY 
 KDM (exchange rate difference): Debit 3,914.50 TRY 
 Therefore, the remaining WRX balance is: 
 1,484,178.26 – 1,480,263.76 = 3,914.50 TRY 
 This amount is exactly the KDM amount. There is also no situation that would cause KDM to operate. 
 The GR and IR quantities are fully matched, so there is no quantity difference for this item. 
 However, when we look at the subsequent periods, we observe that this WRX balance automatically becomes zero in September without any manual clearing for that item. 
 Therefore, our understanding is that this may be a temporary balance caused by the exchange rate difference (KDM) and the fact that different items within the same purchase order are processed in different periods. 
 Is this standard behavior in S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition when KDM is posted due to exchange rate differences? 
 Why does the KDM-related amount temporarily remain as a balance on WRX/GR-IR, even when the GR and IR quantities are fully matched for the item? 
 Is it expected that this balance is automatically cleared in a subsequent period (September)? 
 For the August month-end closing, should we leave these KDM-related WRX balances open and allow the subsequent GR/IR process to clear them? 
 Should MR11 / GR-IR clearing be used for these balances, or should we not clear them manually? 
 Could manually clearing these balances have any impact on Material Ledger / Actual Costing / CKMLCP? 
 Also, w e do not want this behavior in our month-end closing process. Our expectation is that when the GR and IR quantities are fully matched within the same item, the KDM-related difference should not remain as a balance on the WRX/GR/IR account at period end. Is there any standard configuration or BAdI, key-user extensibility option, developer extensibility option, SAP Note/KBA. 
 BR

title: S/4HANA Public Cloud – Standard Business Partner Address Validation Rules
author: Rohit1105
text:
Hi SAP Experts, 
 We are currently using SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud and have integrations in place for Customer and Supplier master data creation and updates from Microsoft CRM and OneTrust . We also have an order integration with our Visit platform , from which we receive addresses for one-time customers. 
 We are currently facing significant challenges with the standard address validations performed by SAP when creating or updating Business Partners . 
 Our source systems are relatively flexible when it comes to address-related fields such as Street, City, Postal Code, Country, Region/State, etc. However, when these Business Partner records are sent to SAP, they can fail because of SAP's standard address validations. 
 For example, we have encountered cases where a US postal code such as: 
 TX78729 
 is rejected by SAP, while: 
 78729 
 is accepted, with an error indicating that the postal code must have a specific length/format. 
 We have already implemented a number of validations on the source-system side based on the errors we have encountered so far and our knowledge of SAP's address requirements. However, we continue to receive new address-related validation errors, particularly when dealing with different countries and regions. 
 The challenge 
 When an address fails validation in SAP, the correction process is currently quite manual and lengthy: 

 The source/admin team receives the SAP error. 

 They contact the SAP team to understand the reason for the failure. 

 The SAP team investigates the error and determines which address rule is being applied. 

 The source/admin team then corrects the address in the source system. 

 The record is resubmitted to SAP. 
 This results in additional manual effort as well as delays in customer/supplier creation or order processing. 
 The situation is expected to become more challenging as we are planning to onboard additional companies, regions and countries onto S/4HANA Public Cloud . As the number of countries and Business Partners increases, we expect the number of address validation issues and the associated manual effort to increase as well. 
 What we are looking for 
 We would like to understand whether SAP provides any documentation, configuration object, table, CDS view, API, standard code reference, or other repository that contains or exposes the standard address validation rules used by S/4HANA Public Cloud. 
 In particular, we would like to understand the rules applied for fields such as: 

 Postal Code 

 City 

 Street 

 House Number 

 Region/State 

 Country 

 Country-specific address formats 

 Mandatory/optional address fields 

 Country-specific formatting or pattern validations 
 Our objective is to obtain the complete set of standard SAP rules for all countries , so that we can implement equivalent validations in our source systems and prevent the records from reaching SAP only to fail during Business Partner creation/update. 
 We are not looking for a custom validation solution or guidance on implementing a BAdI. We are specifically trying to understand the standard validation logic already applied by SAP . 
 We have reviewed the available SAP documentation around Business Partner address validation and Business Address Services, but so far we have not been able to find a single source that provides the complete set of country-specific standard validation rules. 
 Could you please advise: 

 Where are the standard Business Partner address validation rules defined in S/4HANA Public Cloud? 

 Is there a SAP-delivered table, CDS view, API, configuration object, or repository from which we can determine these rules? 

 Is there a complete SAP-maintained list of country-specific postal code/address validation rules? 

 Are some of these validations implemented in standard SAP application logic rather than configuration? 

 Is there any SAP-supported API or service that we can use to validate an address using the same rules that SAP applies during Business Partner creation/update ? 

 If SAP does not expose the complete rules, what is the recommended approach for customers who need to validate large volumes of address data in source systems before sending it to S/4HANA Public Cloud? 
 We would greatly appreciate any guidance or references to the specific SAP objects or documentation where these rules are maintained. 
 Our main objective is to avoid repeatedly resolving address validation errors manually and to establish a sustainable validation process that can scale as we onboard additional companies and countries onto S/4HANA Public Cloud. 
 Thank you in advance for your help.

 The original accounting document and document flow 
 G/L account and company code configuration

 Cost center or profit center assignments 
 Currency and valuation 
 Subledger integration

 CDS-based reporting 
 Data or configuration differences between systems 
 This made me think that S/4HANA FI troubleshooting is becoming less about checking one transaction and more about understanding the complete financial data flow. 
 My questions to experienced S/4HANA Finance consultants:

title: Getting started with Micro-Integrations on Advanced Event Mesh: Access Options & Activation
author: kennethberckmoes
text:
Not every integration scenario requires a full-fledged integration platform. For some scenarios, all you need is a lightweight way to connect an application or service directly to your event broker. 
 This is where the Micro-Integrations capability of SAP Integration Suite, advanced Event Mesh comes in. 
 They provide lightweight integration functionality to easily connect SaaS and legacy applications, LLMs and AI Agents, messaging services, data stores, file servers, etc. directly to your event brokers. It also supports basic transformations, comparable to message mappings. 

 The keyword here is lightweight . Micro-Integrations are not a replacement for Cloud Integration, it complements it. Cloud Integration is designed to handle integration complexity way beyond the level that the Micro-Integrations capability can handle. Micro-Integrations focus on simplicity, speed, and high volume use cases. 
 In practice, using Cloud Integration for simple pass-through scenarios from or to Advanced Event Mesh with no transformation (apart from perhaps a message mapping) can be inefficient. In high-volume scenarios (e.g. Event Streaming) it means you’re consuming a lot of messages without leveraging the true strength of Cloud Integration. 
 This is exactly where the Micro-Integrations capability adds value: handling lightweight, high-throughput integrations, closer to the event broker, while leaving the more complex transformations to Cloud Integration. 
 The following blog: Small but Great: Introducing Micro-Integrations for Advanced Event Mesh was published when Micro-Integrations were released and provides more background on the capability. I recommend reading it before continuing this blog, as it explains the capability and benefits in more detail, this blog focuses specifically on how to obtain access. 
 Initially, included with certain broker service classes (as from Broker 1K), now they are also available an an additional chargeable capability. This new metric you can be charged for each hour an additional Micro-Integration is in state " deployed" , the pricing can be found on SAP Discovery Center . 
 The following table shows how many Micro-Integrations (MI) are included with each broker service class, note that each MI can contain up to 5 flows: 
 Service Class Nr. of Micro-Integrations Included 
 Broker 100 (Developer) 0 
 Broker 250 (Smallest Production Broker) 0 
 Broker 1K 2 
 Broker 5K 5 
 Broker 10K 8 
 Broker 50K 15 
 Broker 100K 25 

 This new (Micro-Integration by the hour) metric enables organizations to: 
 Leverage Micro-Integrations when they only have small brokers: 
 We recommend having the same broker size for PROD and QA. This means that for a 3 tier environment the smallest setup is Broker 250 for PROD and QA and Broker 100 for DEV. In this case, Micro-Integrations are not included in your broker and if you want to use Micro-Integrations, you need to purchase it as a seperate line item. 

 Use additional flows: 
 Every Micro-Integration comes with 5 flows, a single flow contains the details of a target/source system/queue/topic, error handling config (e.g. Dead Message Queues) and a message mapping. 
 So let's say, you have an SFTP source micro-integration, these flows can listen to their own SFTP server or directory/folder and map different objects, for example: 
 5 flows that listen to the same SFTP server but each to a different directory. 
 One listens to the directory /salesorders and maps sales order objects, another one that listens to /businesspartners and maps business partner objects, etc: 
 in this case you require 1 Micro-Integration. 
 5 flows that each listen to a different SFTP server but they both map and publish sales order objects: 
 in this case you require 1 Micro-Integration 
 10 flows that listen to the same SFTP server, but map different objects: 
 in this case you require 2 Micro-Integrations 
 Leverage more Micro-Integrations than included in your Broker or Subaccount: 
 Micro-Integrations cannot be shared across Subaccounts , so let's say you have a 3 tier environment with a 1K Broker in PROD & QA and a 250 Broker (no MIs included) in DEV , each environment is hosted in a different SAP BTP Subaccount. In this case, you can leverage 2 Micro-Integrations in PROD, 2 in QA (as this is included in your Broker), but if you were to use Micro-Integrations on your DEV Subaccount, you would need to activate the entitlement for additional Micro-Integrations on your DEV Subaccount. 
 Following the same example, if you want to use more than 2 Micro-Integrations in your PROD and/or QA environment, you also need to activate the entitlement for additional MIs on your PROD and/or QA Subaccount. 

 In this blog, we will walk you through the process of enabling the Micro-Integrations add-on within your SAP AEM environment, as well as the activation process of a 1K Broker or larger. 
 Assigning the entitlements to your SAP BTP Subaccount 
 In this first part of the blog, we will assign the required entitlements to the SAP BTP Subaccount. Depending on how you want to obtain Micro-Integrations, this can either be the entitlement for the Micro-Integration add-on or an entitlement for a broker service class that includes Micro-Integrations (Broker 1K or larger). 
 This part of the process needs to be done by the Subaccount or Global Account Administrator on SAP Business Technology Platform. 
 Go to your SAP BTP Cockpit 
 Navigate to the SAP BTP Subaccount, where you have deployed an Advanced Event Mesh environment and where you want to enable Micro-Integrations. 

 In your Subaccount, go to " Entitlements ", and click on " Edit ". 

 Now, click on " Add Service Plan " on the right top of the table. 

 Look for " integration-suite-advanced-event-mesh ". 
 Now you should see " SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh ", under "Services available to this subaccount", select this service. 

 Under "Available Plans", select " micro-integration-add-on ". This entitlement allows you to create additional Micro-Integrations beyond those included with eligible broker service classes. 
 Optional: If you want to use the Micro-Integratoins included with your broker service, select the appropriate broker entitlement instead. For example, a Broker 1K includes two Micro-Integrations (this is smallest broker that includes MIs) , please have a look at the documentation if you want to know how many Micro-Integrations are included in your broker. 
 You can also assign both entitlements if you want to use the Micro-Integrations included with your broker service and additional Micro-Integrations through the add-on. 

 Once you've selected the right service plans, click on " Add Service Plans " at the bottom of your screen. 

 Don't forget to press the " Save " button. 

 Optional: Ensure a compatible broker is available 
 To deploy Micro-Integrations, you need at least one active broker in your Advanced Event Mesh environment. If you are using the Micro-Integrations included with a broker service, the minimum service class is Broker 1K . If you are using the micro-integration-add-on entitlement, any broker service class can be used. This section is written for organizations that want to deploy a broker that already includes Micro-Integration. The following steps are performed by the Mission Control Manager in SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh. 
 In your SAP BTP Subaccount, go to " Instances and Subscription " and open " SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh " (under "Subscriptions"). 

 Now, you are redirected to what we refer to as the “ Cloud Console ” in Advanced Event Mesh (you can always go back to the cloud console by clicking on the SAP logo on the top left). 
 In the Cloud Console, scroll down to " Mission control " and open " Cluster Manager ". 

 In the Cluster Manager you seee an overview of your existing brokers. If you don't have a 1K Broker or a larger broker, click on " Create Service" on the right top. 

 Provide at least the following: 
 Service Name 
 Cloud provider & region 
 Service Type: Enterprise 
 Service Class: Broker 1K (or larger) 
 Click on " Create Service ". 

 Once the service is ready, you should see a screen that looks like this (see screenshot below). This means that your broker was successfully created! 

 Granting access to Micro-Integrations 
 If you (or your admin) have successfully configured the appropriate Micro-Integration entitlement and/or broker service, we're almost ready to create and deploy Micro-Integrations. The only thing you must verify is that you and/or the people who should create and deploy the MIs, have the " Micro-Integrations Manager " role assigned. This part of the process is done by the Account Administrator in SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh. 
 In the Cloud Console, click on the user icon (bottom left corner) and go to " Account Details ". 

 Now, go to " User Management " ➡️ " Users ", click on the 3 dots right next to the user you want to grant access to Micro-Integrations and hit " Edit ". 

 Go to the line "Micro-Integrations" and open the drop-down list, select " Micro-Integrations Manager ", and press " Save ". Now this user will be able to create and deploy Micro-Integrations in SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh. Repeat the previous 3 steps to give access to other users. 

 Discovering and creating Micro-Integrations 
 Once the appropriate entitlement has been assigned, a compatible broker is available, and the Micro-Integrations Manager role has been assigned to your user, you can create and deploy Micro-Integrations. 
 In the Cloud Console in Advanced Event Mesh, you should now see a tile with the title " Micro-Integrations ". Click on this tile. 

 Here, you will find an overview of all Micro-Integrations that are created. Click on " Create Micro-Integration " on the right top. 

 Now, you see an overview of all Micro-Integrations that you can create and configure with Advanced Event Mesh. 

 From this list, you can select a Micro-Integration that fits your use case and start configuring it. Configuring a Micro-Integration is very straight forward, you need the connection and credential details of the source or target system, as well as the queue/topic and broker credentials to create and configure the Micro-Integration. 
 If you want to try-out a Micro-Integration, I recommend to go through a blog I wrote earlier this year: 
 File to Mesh: Liberating SFTP Data with Micro-Integrations . 
 In this blog, we create a Micro-Integration that listens to an SFTP server and publishes the lines of a CSV file one by one as (mapped) events to the broker. The File to Mesh use case is one where Micro-Integrations are commonly used.

title: SAP Bydesign– Change of M-User / Tenant Certificate Issuer
author: pangulurivenkata
text:
Symptom 
 Third-party integrations communicating with SAP Business ByDesign (ByD) using M-User / Tenant certificates may experience authentication or communication issues after the certificate issuer is changed, if the new intermediate certificate is not available in the trust store of the external system. 
 Background 
 The certificate issuer for SAP ByD M-User / Tenant certificates is being changed. 
 The issuer will transition as follows: 

 Current 
 New 

 Intermediate Issuer 
 SAP Passport CA G2 
 SAP Cloud Client CA 
 The SAP Cloud Client CA is the new intermediate CA certificate in the certificate chain used for the M-User / Tenant certificate. 
 Important 
 The Root CA certificate remains unchanged . 
 There is no change to the existing Root CA. Only the intermediate issuer in the certificate chain is changing from SAP Passport CA G2 to SAP Cloud Client CA . 
 Timelines 
 The change is tentatively planned for the CMP window of November 14th – 15th 2026 . 
 The exact implementation timing is subject to the final change schedule. 
 Customers are recommended to complete the required trust-store updates before the planned change window . 
 Environment 
 SAP Bydesign 
 Cause 
 If you have third-party integrations that use the SAP ByD M-User / Tenant certificate for certificate-based authentication, the external system may need to trust the new intermediate CA certificate. 
 If the new SAP Cloud Client CA certificate is not available in the relevant trust store, the third-party system may not be able to establish a trusted certificate chain after the issuer change. 
 This can potentially result in authentication or communication failures for the affected integrations. 
 Resolution 
 Action Required 
 If you have third-party integrations using ByD M-User / Tenant certificates, please perform the following actions: 
 Download the SAP Cloud Client CA intermediate certificate from the SAP Global PKI repository: - https://aia.pki.co.sap.com/aia/SAP%20Cloud%20Client%20CA.crt 
 Add/import the certificate into the appropriate trust store / trust list used by the third-party integration. 
 Ensure that the certificate is configured as a trusted intermediate CA certificate. 
 Verify that the SAP Cloud Root CA certificate remains trusted. 
 If applicable, validate the affected integration after importing the new certificate. 
 It is recommended to complete this activity before the November 14th – 15th 2026 CMP window to avoid potential communication disruption when the new issuer becomes active. 
 Certificate Chain 
 Current certificate chain: 
 M-User / Tenant Certificate 
 ↓ 
 SAP Passport CA G2 – Intermediate CA 
 ↓ 
 SAP Cloud Root CA – Root CA 

 Certificate chain after the change: 
 M-User / Tenant Certificate 
 ↓ 
 SAP Cloud Client CA – Intermediate CA 
 ↓ 
 SAP Cloud Root CA – Root CA 

 Only the intermediate CA changes. The Root CA remains unchanged. 

 Frequently Asked Questions 
 What is changing? 
 The intermediate certificate issuer for the ByD M-User / Tenant certificate is changing from 
 SAP Passport CA G2 to SAP Cloud Client CA. 
 Is the Root CA changing? 
 No. The Root CA remains unchanged. Only the intermediate CA issuer is changing. 
 Who needs to take action? 
 Customers with third-party integrations that use or validate the ByD M-User / Tenant certificate should review their integration trust stores and add the new SAP Cloud Client CA certificate. 
 Do I need to remove SAP Passport CA G2? 
 No immediate removal is required as part of this change. 
 Customers should add the new SAP Cloud Client CA certificate to the relevant trust store. The existing SAP Passport CA G2 certificate may be retained to support certificates issued under the existing chain during the transition. 
 Where can I get the new certificate? 
 The SAP Cloud Client CA intermediate certificate can be downloaded from the SAP PKI certificate repository using the link provided below: 
 https://aia.pki.co.sap.com/aia/SAP%20Cloud%20Client%20CA.crt 
 What happens if I do not update the trust store? 
 If the external system does not trust the new intermediate CA, certificate-based communication with ByD may fail once the new issuer becomes active. 
 Does this affect all ByD customers? 
 The impact depends on the customer's integration architecture and whether third-party systems validate the ByD M-User / Tenant certificate chain using a locally maintained trust store or trust list. 
 Customers using such integrations should review their configuration and take the required action. 

 SAP Cloud Client CA – Intermediate Certificate 
 Customers with affected third-party integrations can download the SAP Cloud Client CA intermediate certificate from the SAP Global PKI repository and import it into the relevant trust store/trust list before the planned certificate issuer change. 
 SAP Cloud Client CA certificate: https://aia.pki.co.sap.com/aia/SAP%20Cloud%20Client%20CA.crt

title: Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private - What's New in 2025 FPS02
author: Andrew_Ford
text:
Every upgrade cycle, the gap between available and activated widens, not because teams don't care, but because connecting the dots between what shipped, what it changes, and what you need to do is harder than it should be. SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 FPS02 ships 996 innovations across 15+ lines of business, including 15 AI-embedded capabilities and 622 net-new features , all available now. This post gives you the short version of what matters, where to find the full picture, and how the Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private closes the activation gap for your team. 

 What's New in SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 
 2025 FPS02 ships 996 innovations applicable to SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition, of which 622 are net-new capabilities alongside 345 enhancements to existing functions and 28 deprecations. That breadth spans every major line of business: Finance (150 items), Cross Applications (174), Supply Chain (101), Manufacturing (87), Asset Management (59), R&D/Engineering (53), and more. 

 Not all 996 demand the same attention. Here are five high-impact areas worth reviewing first: 
 1. AI-Assisted Filtering, Error Explanation, and Summarization — embedded in SAP Fiori Elements (App Platform / UX) 
 Three new AI capabilities are now embedded directly into SAP Fiori elements-based applications in Private Edition — exclusively for PE in this release: 
 AI-Assisted Easy Filter : users describe filter criteria in natural language instead of configuring them manually. Particularly relevant for Finance, Procurement, and Planning users working with complex filter sets daily. 
 AI-Assisted Error Explanation : 
 when users encounter an error on an object page, the system explains the issue and recommends resolution steps in plain language. Reduces support escalations and speeds up transaction completion. 
 AI-Assisted Smart Summarization : object pages can generate a contextual summary of the record's contents, useful for approvals, audits, and management reviews. 
 All three are new capabilities in FPS02 and require activation. You can explore all 15 AI-category items for Private Edition directly in the What's New Viewer via this filtered URL: AI/Joule innovations in FPS02 → What's New Viewer . 
 2. Joule API for Web Dynpro Applications (App Platform / ABAP) 
 Web Dynpro apps embedded in the SAP Fiori launchpad can now integrate with Joule via the new IF_WD_JOULE_API interface. This extends Joule's conversational capabilities into legacy Web Dynpro transactions, a significant unlock for customers with custom or older apps still running on Web Dynpro. Available for both SAP S/4HANA and Private Edition. 
 3. AI-Assisted Enterprise Search in Manufacturing 
 AI-assisted natural language search is now available in Production Planning and Control ("AI-Assisted Enterprise Search for Production Planning and Control") and more broadly across manufacturing business data ("AI Assisted Search for Business Data"). Users can query production orders, materials, and resources in plain language without manual search configuration. 
 4. Expanded Joule Capabilities Across the Suite (Cross Applications) 
 The "Joule Capabilities Supported" update in Cross Applications reflects a broader expansion of Joule's transactional coverage. Combined with the new Joule Web Client API for Web Dynpro, this release meaningfully extends the surface area of AI-assisted work available in Private Edition. 
 5. Configuring User Default Parameters for the SAP Fiori Launchpad (App Platform) 
 Administrators can now configure default parameter values for standard and custom SAP Fiori applications via the Launchpad App Manager. Users benefit from pre-populated filter fields without manual setup each session, a targeted improvement for high-frequency transactional roles. Scope: SAP S/4HANA and Private Edition. New capability in FPS02. 
 Customer Action Required vs. auto-on: Of the 996 innovations, 342 are linked to scope items , these are the items most likely to require customer review, activation, or configuration before users benefit. The remaining ~654 are platform-level changes or automatically available post-upgrade. Use the What's New Viewer with the Scope Item filter to generate your team's action list quickly. 

 SAP Best Practices for 2025 FPS02 
 New system capabilities only deliver value when underlying business process designs reflect them. With 2025 FPS02, the SAP Best Practices for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition content library now contains 433 processes in SAP Signavio Process Navigator under the S4O solution scenario , updated to reflect the new and changed functionality in this release. 
 The scope items most affected align with the top innovation areas in FPS02: 
 Finance: Record-to-Report (fixed assets, financial close), Treasury, and Controlling scope items updated to reflect AI-assisted features and API expansions. 
 Asset Management / Maintenance Management: the most extensively updated area in FPS02, with new scope items for Maintenance Order Relationships, Task Planning Design, Industrial System management, and multiple new OData APIs. 
 Service: Call type 6 (Service Order with Advanced Execution) now supported in Manage Maintenance Plans and Manage Maintenance Items apps, moving these processes into the Fiori-native flow. 
 Three process areas to review now: 
 Maintenance Order Relationships: graphical operation sequencing (Asset Management; scope items 4HH, 4HI, BH1, BJ2) 
 The new Manage Maintenance Order Relationships app (F8506) enables graphical visualization and management of operation dependencies within and across maintenance orders. For customers whose maintenance planning spans multiple work centers or requires sequencing logic, this is a process redesign opportunity — not just a new app. Review updated scope items for Reactive, Proactive, and Improvement Maintenance. 
 Service Order with Advanced Execution: Maintenance Plans now in Fiori (Service; scope item 7GA) 
 Previously available only in WebDynpro, call type 6 maintenance plans and items are now manageable in the Fiori-based Manage Maintenance Plans (F5325) and Manage Maintenance Items (F5356) apps. If your team hasn't migrated this process to Fiori, FPS02 removes the final blocker. Review the 7GA scope item for updated process flows and test scripts. 
 Manufacturing AI Search — Production Planning and Control process update (Manufacturing) 
 AI-assisted enterprise search is now embedded in the standard Production Planning process. The scope items for Demand Planning, MRP, and Production Order Management should be reviewed for updated process descriptions that reflect natural language search as a standard workflow step. 
 How to find FPS02 delta content in Process Navigator 
 Navigate to SAP Signavio Process Navigator via SAP for Me → select the S4O solution scenario for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition → filter by release 2025 FPS02. The delta content — updated scope items, new test scripts, revised process flows — is versioned by release and available without a customer system login. 

 Product Enablement 
 The enablement for 2025 FPS02 is available now via the Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private, accessible through SAP Enterprise Support on support.sap.com. 
 What's available today: 
 What's New documentation (version 2025.002) The full What's New content for FPS02 is live on the SAP Help Portal. Each of the 996 items links directly to its help topic, so you can go from innovation description to implementation guidance in one click. The Upgrade Guide for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 (version 3.0, dated October 7, 2026) is published alongside it and covers upgrade prerequisites, simplification items, and deprecated functionality. 
 SAP Signavio Process Navigator — S4O solution scenario As described in Section 2, the S4O scenario in Process Navigator is updated with FPS02 delta content. Process flows, test scripts, and accelerators for scope items with FPS02 changes are live and accessible to S-users via SAP for Me. 
 Release Navigator on Release Ready (support.sap.com) The Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private is available today. It centralizes key dates, feature highlights, scope item links, enablement blogs, and support materials for each release, organized specifically for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition. This is the starting point for anyone who wants to go deeper than this blog post. 
 SAP Learning content No SAP Learning courses have been published specifically for 2025 FPS02 at the time of writing. Existing SAP Learning content for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 covers foundational capabilities and remains relevant as an onboarding foundation for this release. As FPS02 capabilities mature in customer systems, course updates are expected, bookmark https://learning.sap.com and filter to "SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025" to catch new content when it arrives. 
 Who needs system access vs. what's publicly available 
 The What's New Viewer, Upgrade Guide, and Release Navigator content on support.sap.com require an S-user login but not a customer production system. SAP Signavio Process Navigator requires an S-user via SAP for Me. Partners and consultants can access all of this before their customer's system is available, which means there is no reason to wait until upgrade completion to start preparing. 

 Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private 
 The Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private is a curated, role-appropriate digital guide delivered by SAP Enterprise Support. It is built specifically for SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition customers, partners, and consultants, and it solves a concrete problem: the relevant release content is scattered across SAP Help Portal, SAP Community, SAP Learning, and SAP Signavio, and most teams find what they need too late or not at all. 
 Release Navigator pulls this together in one place: key dates, feature highlights organized by line of business, scope item links, release notes, learning assets, and SAP Community blog posts, all filtered to Private Edition and the current release. 
 This tool is built for Private Edition: The Public Cloud release cadence and tooling are different. Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private is scoped and curated specifically for the Private Edition deployment model and the quarterly FPS release rhythm. 
 How to access: Here is a link to the Release Navigator for SAP Cloud ERP Private (S-user required). Partners and consultants with an S-user login — even without a customer system contract — can access the tool and all its FPS02 content directly. 

 Future Planning: 2025 FPS03 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition follows a two-year major release cycle with three Feature Package Stacks (FPS) in between , each FPS delivered approximately every six months. The 2025 base release (FPS00) shipped in October 2025; FPS01 followed in approximately April 2026; FPS02 is generally available as of October 2026. 
 What's next: 
 2025 FPS03 — scheduled for the week of March 1–5, 2027 . FPS03 will be the final FPS in the 2025 release line before SAP's next major base release. 
 SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition 2025 carries mainstream maintenance through December 2032 — giving customers seven years from the base release date to plan their next major upgrade. 
 Why this matters now: If your team is still on an earlier release, FPS02 is the current generally available target. Customers running 2023 FPS02 or earlier should check their maintenance window against SAP's Product Availability Matrix, end-of-mainstream-maintenance dates for older FPS versions are triggered by the availability of newer releases. 
 For forward planning: The SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition innovations roadmap give visibility into planned capabilities before they ship. Teams who review the roadmap before each FPS cycle can pre-configure processes, brief stakeholders, and build test plans in advance, rather than discovering new c

title: Why n8n + SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2 & ESM is a Technical "Match Made in Heaven"
author: Yogananda
text:
My Previous Article: Why n8n Workflows Will Not Replace Solid SAP Integration Suite iFlow Development 
 This article explores the three extensibility capabilities that n8n is uniquely positioned to deliver: 
 External Hooks (zero-code inbound/outbound webhook plumbing) 
 Autoflow (visual, low-code orchestration of multi-step business processes) 
 Event Triggers (real-time reaction to SSC V2 and ESM events without building consumer applications). 

 Together, these capabilities address some of the most common extensibility challenges faced by SAP CX customers tod 
 The Extensibility Challenge in Modern SAP CX Landscapes 
 SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2 already provides a powerful platform for managing customer interactions. Combined with Events, organizations can build highly event-driven architectures that react in real time to business changes. 
 However, many implementation teams still encounter four recurring gaps: 
 Exposing external endpoints often requires custom services or dedicated BTP deployments. 
 Lightweight workflow orchestration is frequently overengineered through traditional integration tooling. 
 AI-driven business processes need rapid experimentation and iteration. 
 Event consumption may require developing and operating dedicated consumer applications. 
 While these challenges are solvable, they often introduce unnecessary complexity and slow down innovation. 
 n8n, embedded natively into Joule Studio on BTP , directly resolves all gaps. 

 Why n8n + SSC V2 & ESM is a Technical "Match Made in Heaven" 
 Architectural Harmony: Where does n8n sit? 
 One of the most important architectural principles is understanding that n8n does not replace your enterprise integration platform . 
 A modern SAP CX landscape benefits from a two-tier integration strategy: ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2 + ESM │
└───────────┬────────────────────────────────┬───────────┘
 │ │
 (Heavy A2A/B2B) (Agile Orchestration)
 ▼ ▼
┌───────────────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────────┐
│ SAP Integration Suite │ │ n8n on BTP │
│ (Core ERP, S/4HANA, EDI) │ │(LLMs, Teams, CRMs, AI)│
└───────────────────────────┘ └───────────────────────┘ 
 In this model: 
 SAP Integration Suite remains the strategic integration backbone for: 
 S/4HANA integrations 
 EDI/EDA/B2B communications 
 Enterprise application integration 
 Governance-heavy integration scenarios 
 Meanwhile, n8n becomes the agility layer for: 
 AI-powered workflows 
 Event-driven automations 
 Rapid SaaS integrations 
 Human-in-the-loop processes 
 Customer engagement enhancements 
 This separation keeps the core stable while enabling business innovation at speed. 
 n8n, embedded natively into Joule Studio on SAP BTP, directly resolves all 3 gaps. The following sections explore each capability in detail. 
 1. External Hooks: Instant Connectivity Without Custom Development 
 The Gap 
 A common requirement in customer service and sales processes is the ability to receive information from external systems. 
 Examples include: 
 Partner applications pushing customer updates 
 Marketing platforms sending lead information 
 Third-party portals triggering service requests 
 AI services submitting analysis results 
 Traditionally, exposing an inbound endpoint on SAP BTP requires: 
 Developing an application 
 Creating deployment artifacts 
 Managing authentication 
 Maintaining lifecycle and operations 
 For many use cases, this is excessive overhead. 
 The n8n Solution 
 The Webhook Trigger node enables teams to instantly expose secure HTTPS endpoints directly within their SAP BTP environment. 
 With only a few configuration steps, organizations can: 
 Receive inbound REST calls 
 Process payloads 
 Apply validations 
 Route requests to SAP APIs 
 Trigger downstream workflows 
 No custom application deployment is required. 
 Example Scenario 
 A reseller portal submits a new sales opportunity. 
 Portal sends data to an n8n webhook. 
 n8n validates the payload. 
 Opportunity is created in SAP Sales Cloud V2. 
 Microsoft Teams notification is posted. 
 AI enrichment is executed automatically. 
 What previously required multiple components can now be assembled visually in minutes. 
 2. Autoflow: Visual Business Orchestration for the AI Era 
 The Gap 
 As organizations expand their AI adoption, business processes become increasingly sophisticated. 
 A typical service scenario may involve: 
 Receiving a customer request 
 Calling an LLM for classification 
 Querying SAP customer data 
 Routing work to a support specialist 
 Waiting for approval 
 Updating SAP objects 
 Notifying external channels 
 While SAP Integration Suite excels at enterprise integration, these human-centric and AI-centric workflows can become cumbersome when implemented solely through traditional middleware. 
 The n8n Solution 
 n8n introduces a visual orchestration layer that is purpose-built for agility. 
 Key capabilities include: 
 Drag-and-drop workflow design 
 400+ prebuilt connectors 
 Native AI and LLM integrations 
 Conditional branching 
 Approval workflows 
 Human-in-the-loop interactions 
 Retry and error handling 
 Business and technical teams can collaborate on workflow design without extensive custom coding. 
 Example: Intelligent Service Escalation 
 When a high-priority complaint is created in Service Cloud: 
 Event received. 
 LLM evaluates urgency and sentiment. 
 Customer history retrieved. 
 Case priority adjusted. 
 Service manager approval requested. 
 Escalation task created. 
 Customer notified automatically. 
 The entire flow remains visually understandable and easy to evolve as business requirements change. 
 This dramatically accelerates innovation while maintaining governance and transparency. 
 3. Event Triggers: Event-Driven Automation Without Consumer Applications 
 The Gap 
 SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2 publishes a rich set of business events when event enablement is activated in the tenant. These events provide real-time visibility into important business activities such as: 
 Ticket/Case created 
 Ticket/Case updated 
 Opportunity changed 
 Lead status updated 
 Account modified 
 Service appointment events 
 Business object lifecycle changes 
 The challenge is not generating the events. The challenge is consuming them. 
 Traditionally, organizations often need to: 
 Develop consumer applications 
 Manage subscriptions 
 Handle message processing logic 
 Operate and monitor custom services 
 Implement retry and error-handling capabilities 
 For many automation scenarios, this becomes unnecessary engineering effort. 
 The n8n Solution 
 n8n provides a low-code event-driven automation layer that can react to business events emitted by Sales and Service Cloud V2 and immediately execute business actions. 
 Instead of building custom applications, teams can visually configure workflows that: 
 Receive business events 
 Filter relevant payloads 
 Enrich context from SAP APIs 
 Execute AI analysis 
 Trigger approvals 
 Notify collaboration tools 
 Integrate with third-party platforms 
 All without writing a dedicated consumer application. 
 Example: Automatic Escalation Workflow 
 When a high-priority service ticket is created: 
 Sales & Service Cloud V2 emits a Ticket/Case Created event. 
 n8n receives the event. 
 Customer history is retrieved. 
 AI evaluates urgency and sentiment. 
 Priority is adjusted automatically. 
 Service manager is notified in Microsoft Teams. 
 Escalation workflow is launched. 
 The entire process can be designed visually and deployed within hours instead of weeks. 
 The Three Extensibility Superpowers of n8n 

 Capability The Challenge n8n Solution 
 External Hooks No lightweight external endpoint available without deploying custom applications Webhook Trigger instantly exposes secure HTTPS endpoints 
 Autoflow AI-driven and human-centric workflows become complex in traditional integration tools Visual orchestration with 400+ connectors, AI nodes, approvals, and wait states 
 Event Triggers Consuming Sales & Service Cloud business events often requires custom development Visual event-driven workflows without building dedicated consumer applications 

 Business Benefits 
 Organizations adopting the SSC V2 + ESM + n8n combination gain several strategic advantages: 
 Faster Time-to-Value 
 New automations can be deployed in hours rather than weeks. 
 AI-Ready Architecture 
 LLMs and intelligent services are integrated directly into operational workflows. 
 Reduced Development Effort 
 Many use cases require configuration rather than custom coding. 
 Improved Agility 
 Business teams can quickly adapt processes as requirements evolve. 
 Clean-Core Compliance 
 Core SAP applications remain untouched, preserving upgradeability and long-term maintainability. 
 Conclusion: Keep the Core Clean, Keep the Innovation Fast The combination of SAP Sales & Service Cloud V2 + ESM with n8n on BTP Joule Studio offers the ultimate competitive advantage for modern IT teams. It honors the "Clean Core" architectural requirement while giving business units the immediate, hyper-agile automation velocity they demand. By using n8n for side-by-side extensibility, you ensure that your customer service operations remain fluid, your sales loops stay tight, and your SAP core remains perfectly upgrade-safe for the future. Watch out for the next blogs on practical use cases using n8n with SSC v2+ESM coming soon.

title: Parallel Valuations: Segmentation Valuation and Financial Chain
author: PreethaB
text:
How do you measure true profitability when value is created across multiple legal entities, plants, countries, and business lines? 
 For many global organizations, this is no longer a theoretical management accounting question - it is a practical challenge that affects standard cost calculation, transfer pricing, margin analysis, and executive decision-making. A material may be produced in one entity, transferred across borders, further processed in another plant, and ultimately sold under a different business line or operating segment. From a legal, group, and management reporting perspective, each view may tell a different story. 
 In my latest blog, I explore how SAP S/4HANA extends parallel valuation with Segmentation Valuation, enabling companies to calculate and analyze costs and margins at additional organizational levels such as operating division and business unit. Using a pharma-inspired scenario, I walk through how segmentation valuation can help organizations better understand value-add across the chain, eliminate internal markups where relevant, and gain a clearer view of net chain margin across business lines. 
 I also touch on Financial Chains in Value Chain Analysis and how this area is expected to evolve further with the planned Financial Chain Valuation Segment capability.

Introduction 
 SAP TechEd is back in Berlin — October 27–29, 2026 at Messe Berlin — and this year's agenda of course circles around agentic AI.  What This Session Is About

 In the hands-on session XP265 you will experience a different approach that overcomes these drawbacks. 
 Spec-driven Development 
 The main idea is to define a specification (or to be precise several specification documents) that capture your intent in detail and store it as markdown files that can be re-iterated upon and reused in other setups like the governance constraints you have in your organization. 
 One further ingredient of this approach is that we support with skills for the AI tool that give you guidance and have the good practices for the setup baked in. 
 In contrast to free-style prompting you can use our skill as commands in the agentic tool of your choice and follow along a structured flow from setting up the governance constraints to defining and detailing your scenario to generating Terraform Code. 
 What will be part of the hands-on workshop

 Do the basic setup of the tooling

 Define the scenario 
 Detail the account setup

 Detail the security setup 
 Detail the connectivity setup 
 Define the tasks

 Generate the Terraform code 
 Deploy the generated Terraform code 
 The foundation for this is “Infrastructure-as-Code Specification Toolkit for SAP Business AI Platform” that is available as open source at https://github.com/SAP/iac-spec-kit-for-sap-business-ai-platform 
 Who Should Attend 
 XP265 is aimed at a dministrators, platform engineers, and architects who are responsible for automating their platform setup . You need to be familiar with BTP concepts like subaccounts, entitlements, directories, etc. Basic Terraform knowledge is not required, but of course an advantage.

title: SAP Cloud ALM Libraries: Your Technical Inventory, Connected to Solution Processes
author: a_schulze
text:
Introduction 
 Which Fiori apps are running in your S/4HANA system? Which are actually being used? And which will be affected by your next upgrade? If the answer lives in a consultant's spreadsheet that went stale after go-live — this post is for you. 
 SAP projects generate enormous amounts of technical knowledge: which apps are in scope, how systems are configured, which custom developments exist, which interfaces connect what. That knowledge is the foundation of every ALM activity — testing, deployment, change management, upgrade planning. Without a place to capture it, it evaporates between phases. 
 SAP Cloud ALM Libraries are that place — and their real value is not just storing apps. It is the ability to cover your entire technical landscape across four dimensions, and connect all of it to your Solution Processes: 

 Application Library — Fiori apps, transactions, and web-based tools running in your system 
 Interface Library — APIs, OData services, integration flows, and technical bridges connecting your landscape 
 Development Library — custom code, BADIs, enhancements, and extensions carrying your specific requirements 
 Configuration Library — system settings, master data configurations, and scenario-dependent setups 

 When all four are connected to your Solution Processes, you move from a flat inventory to a process-level view: which part of your business relies on this interface? Which process will be affected when this custom development is impacted by an upgrade? Which configuration belongs to which scope? This is what makes the difference between a static list and an execution record. 
 The SAP Cloud ALM Best Practice is explicit: Populate Library Elements is a named step in the Discover/Prepare phase — not optional cleanup, but a foundation activity for everything that follows. 

 What Feeds the Library? 
 Depending on where you are in your SAP journey, different sources populate the library: 
 Source When to use Library type 
 SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library (FAL) New implementation — populate apps in scope Application 
 SAP Readiness Check Upgrade or conversion — populate upgrade impact data Application 
 Real User Monitoring (RUM) Operations — enrich with actual usage data Application 
 SAP Solution Manager (SDT) Migration — bring over existing landscape inventory All types 
 Manual / Excel upload Any phase — add custom entries or bulk-edit All types 

 How Libraries Connect to Processes 
 Populating the library is step one. The real value kicks in when you connect library elements to your Solution Processes — because that is what turns a flat inventory into a process-level view of your technical landscape. 
 Each library type connects to SAP Cloud ALM entities differently, and it is worth understanding the model before you start assigning. 
 <<<IMAGE Slide 15 — Library element relations: what each type can connect to (Solution Process, Solution Activity, Requirement, Test Case, Document, etc.)>>> 
 The key distinction is the assignment point : 

 Application and Development are assigned at the Solution Activity level — you do this inside the Process Authoring app, by opening the relevant Solution Activity and assigning the library element there. The process must already be available in Process Authoring (custom or copied from the standard best practice) for Solution Activities to be available for assignment. 

 Configuration and Interface are assigned at the Solution Process level — you do this directly in the Processes app, either by creating the element from within the process or by navigating to the Configuration or Interface tab and assigning it there. 
 One important nuance: Solution Processes are not directly assignable from the Libraries app for any library type. You always navigate from the process side, not the library side. Once assigned, the relation shows up in both places. 

 If you want a broader view — for example, to see which libraries belong to which functional area across projects — you can also assign library elements to Process Hierarchy nodes and view them in Cross-Project Overview → Process Hierarchy Assignments.

The process must already be available in Process Authoring (custom or copied from the standard best practice) for Solution Activities to be available for assignment.

 One important nuance: Solution Processes are not directly assignable from the Libraries app for any library type. You always navigate from the process side, not the library side. Once assigned, the relation shows up in both places. 

 Best Practice: Standard SAP Best Practice processes must first be copied into Process Authoring before Solution Activities become available for library assignment. Processes modeled directly in Process Authoring, imported from Signavio, or created via the Custom Process API are ready to use without this step. 
 If you want a broader view — for example, to see which libraries belong to which functional area across projects — you can also assign library elements to Process Hierarchy nodes and view them in Cross-Project Overview → Process Hierarchy Assignments. 

 The SAP Activate Connection 
 Libraries are active at every phase of the SAP Activate lifecycle: 
 Phase Scenario Key Library Action 
 Discover / Prepare All scenarios Populate library from external sources — FAL, Readiness Check, RUM 
 Explore New implementation Link library elements to Solution Processes in Fit-to-Standard workshops 
 Realize All scenarios Track readiness status; document technical specifications 
 Deploy All scenarios Confirm implemented elements; set Readiness = Implemented 
 Run Operations Enrich with usage data from Real User Monitoring 
 Prepare (Upgrade) Upgrade / Conversion Run Readiness Check → update upgrade impact, identify successors 

 What's Coming in This Series 
 This series uses a single app — F0673 Approve Bank Payments — as a thread through the implementation and upgrade lifecycle. It is one example in the Application Library, but the same principles apply to all four library types. 
 Post 2 — Implementation: Sarah is in a Fit-to-Standard workshop. The team identifies F0673 as the app for their Bank Payment Approval process. She downloads the FAL export and uses a Joule prompt to generate the CALM upload file in minutes. 
 Post 3 — Operations & Upgrade: Six months later, Real User Monitoring confirms F0673 is actively used. Eighteen months later, the Readiness Check flags it as unavailable in the target release — with F0673A as the confirmed successor. Two more Joule prompts handle both upload files. 
 Each post includes a copy-paste Joule prompt you can use with your own export files today — no pre-installed skill required.

title: SAP Expands Joule Assistants and Agents to Advance Autonomous Supply Chain Management
author: Devesh Mishra
text:
Supply chain teams never lack decisions to make. What they increasingly lack is time. 
 SAP Connect in 2026: Advancing the Autonomous Enterprise 

 Read the innovation news guide 

 I’ve spent most of my career building supply chain technology to drive business outcomes at scale. Earlier in my career, nobody was talking about AI. But I was helping build what we’d now call an autonomous supply chain. 

 At scale, manual decision-making simply cannot keep pace with growing consumer expectations. That’s why the next phase of supply chain AI needs to move beyond analysis to help organizations turn insights into action across the processes and applications that move goods. 

 Decision velocity: where supply chain speed is won or lost 

 Even the most intelligent supply chains can struggle to turn a meaningful signal into a well-governed response. I think of that as decision velocity: how quickly an organization can recognize change and coordinate the right response based on relevant business context. 

 In supply chain, decisions are inherently interconnected. Planning affects manufacturing, which depends on product and asset readiness, suppliers, logistics partners, and more. I hear this from our customers today: each decision could be rational; the sum of them was not. 

 AI can automate individual tasks, but isolated intelligence only creates isolated value. 

 Agents need to understand how a decision in one domain affects the next. That’s where supply chain applications become critical, providing the business context, connected processes, and controls that agents need to act. 

 New Joule Agents extend AI across the supply chain 

 This year at SAP Connect, we’re expanding the capabilities of six Joule Assistants introduced earlier at SAP Sapphire and adding specialized Joule Agents that can take on critical supply chain tasks. These capabilities will help organizations respond faster and automate more routine work while keeping people at the center of informed decision-making: 

 The Product Design Assistant will be able to interpret product designs, recipes, and specifications and orchestrate compliant product changes, helping accelerate time to market. 

 The Supply Chain Planning Assistant will help planners sense, simulate, and resolve exceptions in a single workspace, helping teams understand downstream impacts and address disruptions before they ripple across the enterprise. 

 The Manufacturing Assistant will help teams respond to plant-floor disruptions as they happen, while new capabilities in the Logistics Assistant span warehousing, outbound optimization, fulfillment, and transportation dispatching, helping turn logistics insight into action. 

 New agentic capabilities for the Asset Operations Assistant will help translate equipment and maintenance signals into action by supporting the initiation, screening, and simulation of maintenance requests. And the Business Network Assistant will improve collaboration with suppliers and logistics partners in areas such as sourcing, contracting, and exception handling. 

 What connects these scenarios is the ability for agents to operate within the business context already governing the supply chain, so an insight in one area can inform the next and, when authorized, trigger coordinated action. General availability for these new capabilities is planned for Q4 2026. 

 Customer results show autonomy taking hold 

 Customers are already putting this shift into practice. 

 Takeda Pharmaceuticals will use the Supply Chain Planning Assistant to help pinpoint likely causes behind planning issues and propose corrective steps, supporting adaptive planning processes over time. 

 Rebecca Kaufmann, senior vice president and head of Enterprise Platforms at Takeda Pharmaceuticals, said, “We are combining the SAP industry and technology knowledge with our organizational real-life experience. The Supply Chain Planning Assistant will provide us with AI-detected root causes and AI-suggested remediation and also automated performance tracking resulting in a self-healing capability.” 

 Doehler, a global producer of natural ingredients for the food, beverage, life sciences, and nutrition industries, is applying AI to logistics issue resolution. 

 Stephan Schissler, CIO at Doehler GmbH, says, “Our people’s greatest value lies in deciding what to do next—and now they can focus entirely on that. The Logistics Issue Resolution Agent detects the root cause, recommends the resolution, and turns a multi-hour firefight into a one-click decision. Our logistics team has recovered roughly a third of the time once lost to troubleshooting, and our processes are becoming self-resolving rather than exception-driven.” 

 This is how autonomy delivers practical value: moving from manually managing exceptions toward more intelligent supply chain processes. 

 Building autonomy on a foundation of trust 

 As AI takes on a greater role in supply chain decisions, trust must be built into how it operates. Leaders need to understand what AI decided and why, define what it is authorized to complete, intervene when necessary, and know who is accountable. 

 That is the direction behind everything we are introducing at SAP Connect in 2026. By grounding Joule Assistants and their agents in the processes and data of the SAP Supply Chain Management portfolio, we can help organizations move from insight to coordinated action while keeping people at the center of the decisions that matter most. 

 For supply chain leaders, that is where autonomy becomes tangible: less time spent on routine work and resolving exceptions, faster responses when conditions change, and more time for the strategic decisions that strengthen resilience, efficiency and customer value. 

 Ultimately, it comes down to decision velocity you can trust. 

 Devesh Mishra is general manager and chief product officer for SAP Supply Chain Management.

title: SAP Cloud ALM Libraries: Your Implementation Foundation Starts Here
author: a_schulze
text:
In Post 1 we introduced the four library types and the SAP Activate connection. This post walks through the Implementation scenario step by step. 
 The Scenario 
 Julia is a Financial Consultant on an S/4HANA Private Cloud implementation project. During the Finance Fit-to-Standard workshop, the team identifies that the standard SAP Best Practice scope does not cover the customer's Bank Payment Approval process. They create a custom Solution Process — Bank Payment Approval — Finance — and within it a Solution Activity: Implement Approve Bank Payments . 
 The app they need is F0673 — Approve Bank Payments. Sarah now has three tasks: 
 Find the app in the SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library and document it in the Application Library 
 Link it to the Solution Activity 
 Track readiness as implementation progresses 
 Similar illustration. 

 Step 1 — Download the FAL Export 
 Sarah opens the SAP Fiori Apps Reference Library , searches for the F0673, reviews the app details — technical requirements, business roles, and the predecessor/successor info — and uses the Spreadsheet Download feature to export the app data as XLSX. 
 The export contains everything she needs: App Name, App ID, UI Technology, App Description, Product Suite, and Release Version. 

 Step 2 — Use Joule to Build the Upload File 
 Sarah opens Joule Work Desktop, attaches the FAL export, and uses the FAL-to-CALM-Prompt. 
 Joule confirms the file contents, asks for the System Group and Owner, and generates the upload file. 

 Step 3 — Upload and Assign 
 Sarah uploads the file to SAP Cloud ALM → Application Library. F0673 is created with Readiness = Planned . 

 She then opens the Solution Activity Implement Approve Bank Payments in the Process Authoring app and assigns F0673 to it. The full traceability chain is now live: 
 Similar illustration with different values. 

 App → Solution Activity → Solution Process → Requirement → User Story → Test Case → Transport 
 As the project progresses through Realize and Deploy, Sarah updates the Readiness status — from Planned to Partly Implemented to Implemented and tracks the project readiness in the Library Analyitcs app. The library entry becomes the living record of this app from day one. 

 Analytics: Track Implementation Progress 
 The Library Analytics Builder provides a system implementation view: for each System Group (DEV / QAS / PRD), a stacked bar shows Readiness distribution across all library elements. Sarah can see at a glance how many apps in the Finance scope are planned, in progress, or confirmed — and filter by Solution Process to see progress at the business level. 

 Next in this series: Real User Monitoring confirms which apps are actively used — and the Readiness Check identifies which ones need action before the next upgrade. [ Read Post 3 →]
